strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Promotes terminal Completed task/run evidence into an explicit runtime-owned AcceptedComplete state through existing task.run instead of caller-side inference.
Records bounded TaskCompletionAccepted evidence with ids, fingerprints, verifier-gate status, replay state, and next action without raw prompts or provider output.
Requires explicit authorization and rejects non-completed, stale, mismatched, failed-gate, or conflicting acceptance requests before ledger mutation.
Gives headless callers a replay-safe accepted-completion state they can use for later closure, routing, and stop decisions.
Returns bounded completion_acceptance result metadata so callers can distinguish completed, accepted, replayed, and denied acceptance paths.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances agent_loop with persistent structured ledger evidence, runtime_permission_enforcement, headless_autonomous_development, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: Existing task.run can accept a current terminal Completed task/run when the caller supplies explicit completion acceptance authorization, the source run id, an acceptance id, and the expected completion result fingerprint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: TaskCompleted, completion_evidence, verifier gates, and M50 headless journey closure prove completion facts but do not create a durable accepted-completion state owned by the Rust runtime.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless controllers must continue inferring accepted completion from scattered ledger evidence, leaving no finite Completed -> AcceptedComplete transition for autonomous stop and closeout decisions.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.5 replacement, M50.6 closure, and M50.7 uninterrupted journey execution because this is a reusable agent-loop completion state transition, not another Mode Pack route or journey wrapper.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing task.run with a bounded optional completion_acceptance envelope.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase writes and replays bounded acceptance evidence instead of adding a report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust re-reads current task/run state, validates Completed status, source run ownership, bounded acceptance id, terminal completion fingerprint, verifier-gate status, and conflicting accepted evidence before appending TaskCompletionAccepted or replaying an existing AcceptedComplete terminal state duplicate-free.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A scheduled headless caller can now decide follow-on closure or stop behavior from bounded accepted-completion metadata without raw ledger scraping or caller-side acceptance inference.
answers.milestone_progress: This establishes the first M51 finite completion-state transition beyond TaskStatus::Completed and unlocks later headless accepted-completion routing.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M51.1 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a runtime completion-state-machine phase. Review must confirm that guard enforcement is not weakened and that the manifest describes a real accepted-completion state transition rather than a report wrapper.

exit_criteria: task.run accepts one bounded completion_acceptance envelope without adding a new JSON-RPC method
successful acceptance requires authorize_completion_acceptance=true, source_run_id, acceptance_id, and expected_completion_result_fingerprint
runtime re-reads current task/run state and validates Completed status, run ownership, terminal completion evidence, expected fingerprint, and verifier-gate status before ledger mutation
successful acceptance appends one bounded TaskCompletionAccepted event and returns bounded completion_acceptance result metadata
replay of the same acceptance id and fingerprint returns replayed=true without adding another TaskCompletionAccepted or TaskRunning event

a second acceptance request for the same task/run/terminal completion with a different acceptance_id replays the existing AcceptedComplete evidence instead of appending a second TaskCompletionAccepted event
unauthorized, non-completed, mismatched-fingerprint, failed-gate, stale, malformed, or conflicting acceptance attempts fail closed before ledger mutation
VSIX validators accept the bounded request and result shape and reject false authorization, malformed fingerprints, unbounded acceptance ids, unknown raw fields, and raw acceptance payload fields
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, new RPC, VSIX-owned policy, workspace mutation expansion, or broad runtime modularization is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test task_run_completed_task_accepts_completion_once_with_bounded_evidence validates authorized acceptance, bounded result fields, one TaskCompletionAccepted ledger event, raw-data exclusion, same-id replay, and different-id replay of the existing AcceptedComplete terminal state without duplicate acceptance events.
Rust behavior test task_run_completion_acceptance_fails_before_mutation_for_invalid_state_or_fingerprint validates non-completed and mismatched-fingerprint denial before ledger mutation.
Rust behavior test task_run_completion_acceptance_denies_failed_gate_and_conflicting_replay validates failed verifier-gate denial and conflicting accepted evidence denial without mutation.

VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests validate completion_acceptance request/result shape, false authorization rejection, malformed fingerprint rejection, unknown request field rejection, and raw result field rejection.

accepted_capability: Runtime-owned AcceptedComplete transition for terminal Completed task/run evidence through existing task.run
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime task_run_completed_task_accepts_completion_once_with_bounded_evidence -- --nocapture validates the positive end-to-end acceptance plus same-id and different-id replay paths.

cargo test -p brownie-runtime task_run_completion_acceptance -- --nocapture validates denial paths for non-completed, unbounded acceptance id, mismatched fingerprint, failed gate, and conflicting accepted evidence.
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix test -- runtimeClient.test.ts validates the VSIX protocol guards for the new task.run envelope, bounded acceptance id, and result metadata.
safety_boundary: completion_acceptance requires explicit authorize_completion_acceptance=true and cannot be combined with task-run context materialization fields
acceptance_id must be 1-48 ASCII alphanumeric, dash, underscore, colon, or dot characters
acceptance is limited to an existing terminal Completed task whose current run id matches source_run_id
expected_completion_result_fingerprint must match current bounded terminal completion evidence
present or required verifier completion gates must be Passed before acceptance

existing AcceptedComplete evidence is unique per task/run/terminal completion; a different requested acceptance_id replays the existing accepted terminal state and conflicting existing evidence fails closed before mutation
ledger and RPC acceptance metadata contain only ids, status strings, SHA-256 fingerprints, verifier-gate status, replay state, and next action
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only wrapper
No automatic acceptance without explicit authorization
No provider execution, tool execution, verifier retry, patch apply, workspace mutation, shell, git, network, or service expansion
No Mode Pack route, Golden Journey route, or headless.run.drive expansion in this slice
No broad behavior-preserving split of crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs
rejected_alternatives: Adding a new task.acceptCompletion RPC was rejected because existing task.run already owns terminal replay and completion evidence reconstruction.
Adding another completion report/history/verdict/readiness endpoint was rejected because M51 needs a state transition and ledger mutation.
Letting callers infer accepted completion from TaskCompleted plus verifier evidence was rejected because it leaves acceptance outside Rust runtime authority.
Broad runtime modularization was deferred to future cohesive domain PRs so this product slice remains reviewable and independently testable.
technical_debt: crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large; future module extraction should be cohesive, low-dependency, and independently buildable/testable.
Headless routing does not yet consume AcceptedComplete state; M51.2 should connect this state to run-control closure decisions.
The accepted-completion state currently appears as bounded ledger/result evidence rather than a new TaskStatus variant to avoid widening task lifecycle semantics in this first slice.
next_capability_rationale: M51.2 should route AcceptedComplete through headless.run.drive or run-control results so autonomous callers can close or stop only after runtime-owned accepted completion.
Later M51 phases can add product completion DoD gates over AcceptedComplete without replacing this ledgered transition with a report wrapper.
